root_cause: Single-shot harness never executes the draft, so empty-result/wrong-projection errors (bad join keys, wrong literals, over-narrow SELECT) go undetected despite a spare policy call
what: Adds an execute-and-repair stage: run the draft SQL, and if it errors or returns zero rows, send the model concrete diagnostics (error text, actual stored values matching quoted literals, declared FKs, which WHERE predicate kills all rows) plus a focused checklist for a second corrected query; also adds prompt rules on join keys/literals and on selecting all entity columns for 'which X' questions.

root_cause: No execution feedback: silently-empty queries from wrong string literals/filters are returned unchecked
what: Execute the drafted SQL; if it errors or yields zero rows, spend the second policy call on a repair turn containing the error/empty-result signal and instructions to probe actual stored values. Add general prompt rules for literal matching (case/whitespace/partial text) and for selecting all entity columns when the question names no specific attributes.
decision: s2 improves the evolve score from 83.33 to 86.67 with a general, domain-agnostic mechanism (execute-and-repair on error/empty results plus literal-matching prompt rules) rather than task-specific hacks; the single regression (sp0600) is outweighed by two fixes and the token increase stays within admissibility.

root_cause: Execution feedback only fires on error/zero rows, so non-empty but wrong results (join-fanout duplicates, under-projection) are never checked; prompt rules for DISTINCT and entity-wide SELECT * are too weak
what: Extend the repair trigger: run a duplicate-row probe on any successful draft that contains JOIN/UNION and lacks DISTINCT/GROUP BY/aggregates/LIMIT, and if exact duplicate rows exist send a second-call feedback telling the model to deduplicate with DISTINCT (or fix join fan-out). Also strengthen two general prompt rules: use DISTINCT whenever joins can repeat an entity in a list question, and select all columns of the entity table when the question asks 'which/show <entities>' without naming attributes. These target sp0536/sp0600 (duplicates) and sp0755 (projection); no task-specific logic.

root_cause: Silent row-multiplicity errors: join fan-out duplicates are never checked because the harness only reacts to execution errors and empty results
what: Adds a duplicate-row detector: when a draft executes fine but returns exact duplicate rows (a classic one-to-many join fan-out), spend the second call on a repair turn that shows the duplicated rows and asks for DISTINCT / de-duplicated joins unless multiplicity is genuinely requested. Also adds a general projection rule covering gold-style `SELECT *` over all joined tables for whole-entity questions.

root_cause: Repair feedback only fires on error/zero rows, so non-empty join-fanout duplicate results (wrong row multiplicity) are returned unchecked
what: Reuse the existing single execution result to detect exact duplicate tuples in drafts containing JOIN/UNION without DISTINCT/GROUP BY/aggregates/LIMIT; when found, spend the second policy call on a repair turn showing the duplicated rows and asking for a semantic decision (keep if duplicates are legitimate, otherwise DISTINCT/EXISTS/correct grain), accepting the repair only if it executes. Also strengthen the projection rule so bare 'which <entities>' questions select all columns of the entity.

root_cause: Execution feedback only reacts to errors/empty results, so join fan-out duplicates silently inflate the row multiset of otherwise-correct queries
what: Add a legal-SQL duplicate probe (COUNT(*) vs COUNT(*) over SELECT DISTINCT * of the wrapped draft) for plain joined SELECTs without DISTINCT/GROUP BY/aggregates/LIMIT, and fix detected fan-out deterministically by injecting DISTINCT into the outer select list, accepting it only if it still executes with the deduped row count. This removes the invalid-SQL bug of r1s1 and the costly, destabilizing second policy call of r1s2.
